passage:
Sudha was shelling peas on the verandah when her phone buzzed: a group photo from the riverbank, six friends with jalebi and a cricket bat, Tanvir grinning in the middle. Nobody had told her about it. The peas went into the bowl faster, and her throat felt tight. So they don't want me now, she thought.

She put the phone down, finished the peas and listened to a bus honking on the main road. Then she picked it up again and typed to Tanvir: "Saw the riverbank photos. It stung a bit that I wasn't there. Was it planned for a reason?"

Tanvir called within minutes. "It was Rafiq's cousin's plan, and we got roped in at the bus stand. I should have called you. Come next Sunday, we're going again."

Sudha smiled at the peas, still stung, but lighter.

qa.q: What were the friends holding in the riverbank photo?
How did Sudha feel on seeing the photo, and how can you tell?
qa.a: She felt hurt and left out, thinking her friends no longer wanted her; her throat felt tight and the peas went into the bowl faster.

qa.q: What did Sudha do that helped, compared with assuming the worst?
qa.a: She let herself feel the sting, then asked Tanvir directly and calmly, which gave room for a kinder explanation.

qa.q: How did Tanvir see the gathering?
qa.a: As an unplanned outing that came together at the bus stand, and Tanvir regretted not calling Sudha.

grounding: Sudha sees photos of a gathering she was not invited to, feels the sting, and asks directly instead of assuming malice.

passage:
"Zainab, got a minute?" Yusuf held the canteen door open. "I saw the photos from Saturday. The biryani night at your place."
Zainab winced. "Ah."
"I'm not trying to make it a thing. It just stung, seeing all of us minus me. Did I do something?"
"No! God, no." She sat down. "It was my cousin's farewell, mostly her friends. I only asked people who already knew her. I didn't think it would look like... that."
"It did look like that." Yusuf managed a laugh. "I spent all Sunday wondering if everyone secretly hated me."
"I'm sorry. I should've mentioned it to you before posting."
"Thanks. Honestly, I almost unfollowed you all at 2 a.m. Glad I asked instead."
"Next biryani night, you're on onion duty."
"Deal. I cry at onions anyway."

qa.q: What was the gathering in the photos?
qa.a: A biryani night at Zainab's place, for her cousin's farewell.

qa.q: What was Yusuf worried about all Sunday?
qa.a: Hurt and anxious, he wondered whether everyone secretly hated him.

qa.q: Which choice worked for Yusuf, and why?
qa.a: Asking Zainab directly instead of unfollowing everyone at 2 a.m.; it showed there was no malice behind the guest list.

qa.q: How does Zainab see the photos after Yusuf speaks?
qa.a: She realises they looked like exclusion and feels sorry she didn't mention it before posting.

grounding: Shows seeing photos of a gathering you were not invited to, feeling the sting, and asking directly instead of assuming malice.

passage:
Last month I saw Uday's story from Rishikesh: six of our class on a raft, helmets on, screaming happily. I hadn't even known there was a trip.
I didn't ask anyone. I left the class group that night and posted a song about fake friends. Very mature. For a week I sat at the other end of the lecture hall and let everyone wonder.
Then Uday stopped me outside the library. "Why did you leave the group?" I said, "You know why." He looked genuinely lost. It turned out the trip had been planned in a different chat for the NSS volunteers, and all six were NSS. I'm not. Nobody had thought of it as a class trip.
It still stung a little. But the week of silence had hurt more than the trip ever did, and I'd made it harder for everyone. Next time, I want to ask first and sulk later, if at all.
— Zeenat

qa.q: What was Zeenat feeling when leaving the class group?
qa.a: Hurt and resentful, assuming the others had deliberately left Zeenat out.

qa.q: What went wrong, and what could fix it next time?
qa.a: Zeenat assumed the worst and retaliated with silence and a pointed song; asking directly first would have shown it was an NSS trip, not a snub.

qa.q: How did Uday experience Zeenat's week of silence?
qa.a: Confused and lost, not knowing why Zeenat had left the group.

grounding: Illustrates being left out of a trip, assuming the worst and retaliating, and learning to ask directly because it may not be malice.
